title: Maintenance Window Planner — tenant-aware upgrade timeline and cost-preview microflows
creator: Asha Patel
description: Prototype and UX spec for a Maintenance Window Planner in the Private/VPC Console. The planner allows operators to schedule cluster upgrades and maintenance with tenant-aware lanes, live cost-impact preview, SLO-aware recommended windows, and clear rollback/canary controls. Goal: reduce upgrade-induced outages and make cost/latency trade-offs explicit to platform and tenant owners.
acceptance_criteria: Planner shows per-tenant lanes with estimated outage and performance impact for a chosen maintenance window
Cost-preview calculates incremental token and infrastructure cost for scheduled operations and shows a 7-day forecast
Canary window slider and automatic rollback options are available and wired to existing rollout objects in the backend
RBAC hides tenant-identifying metadata from viewers without Tenant-Read permission and surfaces an audit-log link
Design spec includes annotations for accessibility, keyboard flows, and microinteraction timing for alerts and toasts
design_notes: Primary view is a timeline with rows representing tenant groups (by SLA tier) rather than individual tenants to avoid information overload
Left column contains a compact cluster summary (node pool impact, expected downtime percentage, affected services list)
Cost-preview panel is collapsible; default suggestion shows both absolute ($) and relative (%) cost change during the maintenance window
SLO-awareness: integrate recent 30-day p50/p95 latency and error rates to recommend low-impact windows; recommendations appear as badges on day cells
Prototype includes an exploratory microflow where a user toggles 'Apply quantization profile' to see changes in both compute time and risk score
decisions: Surface tenant groups instead of raw tenant names to balance operator visibility and privacy
Show recommended windows computed from historical traffic and SLO metrics; final scheduling still requires human confirmation
Place cost-preview to the right of timeline to maintain spatial mapping between window selection and cost delta
Keep canary controls inline with each tenant group for fast local rollouts; global canary actions are in a dropdown
tradeoffs: Detailed per-tenant visibility vs. privacy: chose grouped lanes to avoid exposing PII while keeping actionable granularity
Realtime cost calc uses sampled telemetry to avoid expensive queries — trades absolute precision for fast UI feedback
Inline controls reduce click-throughs but increase cognitive load; addressed with progressive disclosure and tooltips

notes_summary: Prototype prioritizes quick scheduling workflows, tenant privacy, and cost transparency. Next steps: backend preflight contract, implement RBAC redaction, run 3 moderator usability sessions, then handoff to Eng for spike implementation.
